header.name: Ubiquitous Computing
header.description: The course offers a comprehensive introduction to Ubiquitous Computing, in which the students can learn about the seamless integration of computing techniques in the environment. The course on this emerging field is focused on the basic principles, methodologies, and applications of Ubiquitous Computing. It focuses on ambient and context-aware computing, location and motion sensing, and physiological sensing. Along with the principles and methodologies of Ubiquitous Computing, the students will explore the scope and design of real-world applications that sense, process, and respond seamlessly based on the user's context. Through hands-on activities and assignments, the students will be familiarised with sensors, conceptual designs of assistive systems, data, data processing, and visualization; some of the key components of Ubiquitous Computing. The course also includes an understanding of Affective and Wearable computing through case studies, discussions, and hands-on experiments.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be introduced to the basics and concepts of Ubiquitous Computing. They will be able to comprehend its emergence, context and importance in the society.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be familiarized with the scope, resources, modalities and techniques of Ubiquitous Computing. They will be able to correlate this knowledge to real-world problems.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply the knowledge of Ubiquitous Computing techniques, modalities and processes to applications and produce research ideas.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to understand, evaluate and criticise existing Ubiquitous Computing and design soutions and will be able to propose and justify alternate solutions.
